title: WHY GOD SENT HORNETS BEFORE SENDING SOLDIERS
paragraphs: WHY GOD SENT HORNETS BEFORE SENDING SOLDIERS
The Battle God Won Before Israel Arrived
By Gospel Warrior
Most people imagine God's victories arriving with thunder.
Trumpets.
Armies.
Walls collapsing.
Kings falling.
The dramatic moment everyone remembers.
But hidden in the shadows of Israel's conquest lies one of the strangest military strategies recorded in Scripture.
God sent hornets.
Not swords.
Not chariots.
Not soldiers.
Hornets.
Before Israel ever arrived on the battlefield.
Before they drew their weapons.
Before they fought their wars.
God was already fighting theirs.
And if you understand why God sent hornets before sending soldiers, you may finally understand what God has been doing in your own life long before you recognized His hand.
The verse is easy to miss.
Buried within God's covenant promises is a statement that sounds almost unbelievable.
In Exodus 23:28, God declares:
"And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee."
The Hebrew text reads:
וְשָׁלַחְתִּי אֶת־הַצִּרְעָה לְפָנֶיךָ
Ve-shalaḥti et-ha-tsir'ah lefanekha.
Literally:
"And I will send the hornet before you."
The word צִּרְעָה (tsir'ah) refers to a stinging insect, commonly translated as hornet.
The same promise appears again in Deuteronomy 7:20 and Joshua 24:12.
Three separate times.
God wanted Israel to remember this detail.
Because the hornets were never merely about insects.
They were about sovereignty.
They were about preparation.
They were about God moving before His people could even see the battlefield.
Imagine being a Canaanite farmer.
One day life feels normal.
The next day fear spreads through the region.
Strange disruptions begin.
Communities become unsettled.
People abandon strongholds.
Morale collapses.
Panic grows.
The Hebrew Scriptures repeatedly connect the hornets with terror and divine dread sent ahead of Israel.
God was destabilizing resistance before His people ever arrived.
Joshua later reminds the nation:
"I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow."
Joshua 24:12
Not with your sword.
Not with your bow.
Not because of your strength.
Not because of your brilliance.
Not because of your strategy.
God was dismantling obstacles before Israel could claim credit for removing them.
That truth collides head-on with human pride.
Because we love victories that showcase us.
God often prefers victories that showcase Him.

The ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament, known as the Septuagint, translates hornet using the word σφηκία (sphēkia), referring to a stinging wasp-like insect. Yet the emphasis remains the same.
The power was never in the insect.
The power was in the God who sent it.
Throughout Scripture, God repeatedly works this way.
Before David ever faced Goliath, God was already preparing a shepherd in hidden fields.
Before Joseph ruled Egypt, God was already positioning circumstances through betrayal, slavery, and imprisonment.
Before Moses delivered Israel, God was already preserving his life in a basket floating through the Nile.
Before Jesus began His public ministry, God was already orchestrating centuries of prophecy.
God moves before His people move.
That is one of the most comforting and terrifying truths in the Bible.
Comforting because God is ahead of us.
Terrifying because we often don't recognize His activity until much later.
Many believers spend years praying for open doors while missing the fact that God is already removing walls.
They pray for visible miracles while God is performing invisible preparation.
They ask for armies.
God sends hornets.
The promotion you eventually received may have started with conversations you never heard.
The breakthrough you celebrated may have begun through disappointments you hated.
The relationship that changed your life may have been prepared through seasons of loneliness you could not understand.
The rescue may have started long before the crisis arrived.
God's greatest works often happen where human eyes cannot see.
That pattern reaches its ultimate expression in Jesus Christ.
Long before the cross stood on Golgotha, God was preparing redemption.
Long before Bethlehem, prophets spoke.
Long before prophets spoke, promises were made.
Long before promises were made, God already knew humanity would need a Savior.
Scripture describes Jesus as:
"The Lamb slain from the foundation of the world."
Revelation 13:8
Before humanity fell.
Before history unfolded.
Before sin spread.
God already had a plan.
The hornets were pointing toward something larger.
A God who prepares salvation before people recognize their need for it.
A God who fights battles before His children understand they are in danger.
A God who moves first.
Always.
This changes how we view unanswered prayers.
Maybe Heaven has not been inactive.
Maybe Heaven has been sending hornets.
Maybe God is already disturbing what needs disturbing.
Maybe He is already weakening what needs weakening.
Maybe He is already dismantling what needs dismantling.
Maybe the battle you fear has already begun to shift in ways you cannot yet measure.
The greatest mistake Israel could have made was assuming they were alone because they could not see God's activity.
We make the same mistake.
We assume silence means absence.
Delay means abandonment.
Waiting means inactivity.
Yet Scripture repeatedly reveals a God who works ahead of His people.
Even now.
Especially now.
Somebody reading this is exhausted because nothing seems to be changing.
You've prayed.
You've waited.
You've cried.
You've questioned.
And it feels as though Heaven has gone quiet.
But what if the hornets have already been released?
What if God is doing something behind the curtain that your current perspective cannot yet see?
What if the battlefield is already changing?
What if the resistance is already weakening?
What if your future victory began months ago?
Years ago?
Maybe before you were even born?
Because the God of Scripture is not merely present in your battles.
He goes before them.
That is why Israel's story was never ultimately about military conquest.
It was about trust.
Would they believe God was working before visible evidence appeared?
That remains the question for us.
Can you trust God when you cannot yet see the hornets?
Can you trust Him when preparation is hidden?
Can you trust Him when victory is still invisible?
Faith begins where sight ends.
And sometimes the greatest miracle is not the army God sends.
Sometimes it is the hornets He sent long before the army ever arrived.
Be honest. This hit harder than you expected.
And never forget:
The God who stands beside you is the same God who already arrived before you.
